types.Region: abstract directional/speaker place owner, no country or coordinates

types.HeatProfile: intensional pair(region,season), not scalar measurement or event
types.MaterialKind: generic V; never a single cross-case material witness
types.WeatherVapourClass: MaterialKind plus explicit outcome fitness restriction
types.RaiseRequirement: agent HeatProfile plus explicit qualified material and optional height goal
types.PropertyData: typed predicate description, only asserted through its written predication production
types.NominalData: Type union (not an added runtime wrapper): Region, Season, HeatProperty data, ComparisonNominal, AccountPattern. THE preserves the selected member type.
types.Prop: complete source-qualified proposition, distinct from all nominal/data types
types.Coord: Coord[T] is a typed sequence wrapper. OR admits exactly T in WeatherVapourClass,RaiseRequirement,Prop. OTAR separately admits WeatherKind. Boolean/class/inability interpretation is supplied only by the declared consumer.
types.AccountPattern: generic weather content under region/season, not actual event history
types.Reference: always retains listed sort/owner; unknown literals never supply a binder
types.AccountPatternNominal: Syntactic category only; semantic denotation is exactly AccountPattern. No different semantic sort or implicit cast.
types.TopicDescription: In this grammar the admitted nominal topic is AccountPattern. Physical GoalDescription is a different type and uses the separately paid TO interface.
types.PremiseData: Tagged Prop or ClimateContext under GIVEN; G03 consumes Prop and G12 consumes ClimateContext. Neither tag can substitute for a WeatherKind.
types.ConsideredArgument: Wrapper retaining exactly its input ArgumentData content tag. Only G06 extracts an explicitly marked comparison pattern, and G12 packages a complete reason as ExplanationArgument.

morphology.no_confirmation: Cuts and meanings chosen jointly on already exposed data. Operation is a real unchanged calculation but its target binding has no independent support.
morphology.prediction_limit: Replacing either Season input changes the complete profile and all bare-root statements; replacing the explicit region changes its owner. grammar.name: Literal types and references
grammar.signature: typed lexical denotation -> same typed denotation
grammar.rule: Every whole literal has the one lexicon value above. No approximate spelling, case deletion, entity normalization or alternate-reader alias. A KindReference is not an actual parcel; a Property is data awaiting its declared predication rule. Every reference needs its explicit earlier introduction, except local climate fields resolved by G02 within one complete constituent.

grammar.name: Finite climate and account scope
grammar.signature: ClimateContext = {region:Region,season:Season,theme:Kind}; Account = finite explicit claims attached to that context
grammar.rule: The explicit context selectors in the lexicon establish c0,cs0,cES,cEW,cW. A written region or season may be supplied later inside the SAME declared finite account; pending fields must unify at closure, never with a later unrelated account. HeatProfile(r,s) is an intensional profile description, not an event or measured quantity. shedy reads HeatProfile of the selected context. Each written reference and projection therefore retains region and season. Partial reader rows cannot import a ZL binder. The initial opaees introduction establishes page theme V. New ordinary Region/Season contexts preserve that already written theme; LOS explicitly replaces it with THUNDER only in cW, and OCHAR explicitly restores the opening theme V. This copy/select policy is a paid scope convention, not target-derived punctuation.

grammar.name: Question premise and relatives
grammar.signature: GIVEN(Prop), ASK(GIVEN(Prop),Question)
grammar.rule: A kind introduction followed by its theme reference supplies the antecedent to WHICH GENERATES WeatherKind-coordination. A subsequent RISES DURING_RANGE BOTH Season Season supplies the ascent premise. Generates/rises here are generic kind predications. odeedy keeps one anticipated Question open through the complete C02 comparison; it does not assert that a person actually asked. GIVEN has the explicit tagged instance Prop -> PremiseData[Prop] here; OTAR returns Coord[WeatherKind], a domain distinct from the three OR domains.

grammar.name: Typed coordination
grammar.signature: Coordinate[T](x1,...,xn) -> Coord[T], n>=1; T in WeatherVapourClass,RaiseRequirement,Prop
grammar.rule: or is prefix or infix coordination. Parenthesized constituents in the manual AST fix attachment. Nested Coord[T] flattens only at identical T. Unary coordination is explicitly permitted and semantically retains its sole operand; this paid freedom is used in C09/C11/C13. No cross-category coordination or implicit subtype exists. Consumers are explicit: G09 takes class union; G18 distributes inability; G05 folds Coord[Prop] with conjunction. otar and ary are separate paid coordinators for WeatherKind and class modifiers.

grammar.name: Assertion and proposition coordination
grammar.signature: ASSERT(Prop)->Prop; Fold(Coord[Prop])->Prop
grammar.rule: chey may precede a complete Prop or follow its complete predicate application. This is one denotation with two paid surface positions. Prop coordination is conjunction. Nominal descriptions, properties and argument records do not automatically become propositions.

grammar.name: Anticipated comparison
grammar.signature: THUNDER_PATTERN(Context)->ContextualThunderPattern; WHY_NOT_AS(Pattern,Pattern)->Question
grammar.rule: odar applied to aloees or octhody gives the two contextual patterns. qotedaiin marks the second as comparison member. CONSIDER is a discourse wrapper over tagged ArgumentData and preserves its contained Question/ComparisonArgument/ExplanationArgument; wrappers can be nested but do not supply missing operands. G06 reads those explicit wrappers, rather than casting an arbitrary object to a question. NOT_AS remains a qualitative comparison, not a universal zero-winter-thunder claim. The type interfaces are explicit: qotedaiin maps Pattern -> ArgumentData[ComparisonArgument]; CONSIDER maps ArgumentData[t] -> ConsideredArgument[t]. WHY_NOT_AS accepts a Pattern as first argument and a marked or ConsideredArgument[ComparisonArgument] as second, extracting only its expressly contained Pattern. Its Question output is injected by this production into ArgumentData[Question] for the outer CONSIDER. This is a paid finite interface, not a global transparent cast.

grammar.name: Nominal determination and ranges
grammar.signature: THE(NominalData[T])->NominalData[T]; BOTH(x,y)->Pair[T]
grammar.rule: NominalData has the explicitly admitted tags Region,Season,PropertyData,ComparisonNominal,AccountPatternNominal. THE is identity and preserves the tag. BOTH takes exactly two explicit same-sort values, or an explicit pair reference. ACROSS takes the stated opening case pair; it does not quantify over all regions. NominalData is a union of the underlying denotation types, not an extra wrapper requiring a silent coercion.

grammar.name: Rhetorical comparison topic
grammar.signature: TO(AccountPattern(OF Season)) + Comparison(WITH ascent Prop, ACROSS pair) -> TopicArgument
grammar.rule: This construction produces a discourse topic referring back to the written Question, not a new weather assertion. shedaiin TO has two listed interfaces: TopicDescription here, GoalDescription in G17. The difference is paid; no general coercion from topic to physical goal. C03 is an explicitly redundant restatement of C02, not an extra scientific observation. OLAIIN is the same Pattern(context) builder in both uses: OF Season supplies the season with the already written current region; the bare G24 use supplies the already complete current context. The nominal syntactic name is not a second semantic type.

grammar.name: Residual winter outputs
grammar.signature: SUN + Coord[WeatherVapourClass] + RAISES + DURING Season -> RaisingClaim
grammar.rule: aiin/opchdy and qotor/sheedy make two classes of the same generic V fitted for rain and snow. shodaiin with olfar ary dair sheo makes the wind/fire alternative; NOT_CALLED_LIGHTNING restricts fires only. Prefix or or gives a three-member class coordination. Its denotation is a union of alternative vapour classes; it does not make one parcel produce every weather kind. During WINTER resolves to c0, already explicitly introduced. ARY denotes disjunction/union of the wind and restricted-fire fitness classes, not an intersection demanding both products from one portion.

grammar.name: Only that output class
grammar.signature: ONLY(SUCH(KIND(RaisingClaimRef))) -> Prop
grammar.rule: roseer reads the immediately preceding closed Sun RaisingClaim. KIND/SUCH project exactly its explicit object-class union. ONLY adds the source restriction on winter lifting to that union; it does not negate every weather event. Subject, region and season are retained from that written claim.

grammar.name: Attribution and regional cases
grammar.signature: SOME_SAY(RegionalAccount)->AttributedProp
grammar.rule: pchedeey introduces reported speaker group SOME_PEOPLE; olkey introduces EAST and the following SUMMER establishes cES. NO negates THUNDERS in that context. Later explicit rE selectors preserve this attribution; RETURN_TO_OPENING exits it. WEST inherits the same regional-report attribution as an explicitly paid scope choice. The source boundary of the last western statement remains qualified, not an independent observation.

grammar.name: Explanation and setting contrast aside
grammar.signature: CONSIDER(EXPLAINED(ClaimRef, BECAUSE(reason Prop,contrast context))) -> ArgumentData[ExplanationArgument]
grammar.rule: The preceding absence is the explicit explanandum. THE EAST + WINTER, SET_ASIDE AS_CONTRAST names cEW as comparison context without asserting its weather yet. GIVEN EAST SUMMER USE_THIS_CONTEXT selects cES for the reason. No equality of winter and summer heat follows. The later complete heat/process conjunction provides the reason Prop. EXPLAINED packages the linked reason as ArgumentData[ExplanationArgument] for CONSIDER; this packaging is explicit and preserves the target ClaimReference. GIVEN has its second paid instance ClimateContext -> PremiseData[ClimateContext] here. EAST+SUMMER with the explicit selector constructs that context before GIVEN packages it; it is not being silently asserted as a weather Prop.

grammar.name: Internal thermal-profile constructor
grammar.signature: F: Season -> (Region -> HeatProfile); F(s)(r)=HeatProfile(r,s)
grammar.rule: The exact internal component qo has ONE value F, licensed only when the complete remainder is a member of the frozen Season-root domain {dar,daiin}. dar=SUMMER and daiin=WINTER. Thus qo|dar computes a SUMMER-specialized builder; qo|daiin a WINTER-specialized builder. A region is still mandatory. No whole spelling is consulted to choose an output or causal effect. All other qo substrings/forms are residual wholes and are exhaustively listed separately.

grammar.name: Heat builder application
grammar.signature: HeatProfileBuilder RegionRef -> HeatProfile
grammar.rule: qodar qotedar computes HeatProfile(rE,SUMMER); qodaiin odain computes HeatProfile(r0,WINTER). These are ordinary function applications with written arguments. There is no automatic positivity, benefit, sufficient-condition claim or weather result in F.

grammar.name: Heat properties and multiple processes
grammar.signature: HeatProfile + HeatProperty + ProcessPredicate MaterialKind + PreventionPredicate Transition -> Prop
grammar.rule: qokar predicates Excessive of the computed heat. qotchd predicates Disperses with that SAME explicit heat as agent and qotom as V. soiis retains that heat as agent for prevention. Shared subject attachment is licensed only within this contiguous predication chain and cannot cross a new subject/context selector. The reason is the conjunction of these qualified predicates, not an assumed temporal update.

grammar.name: Source causal ownership
grammar.signature: BECAUSE(target,AND(Excessive(H),Disperses(H,V),Prevents(H,ThickenToCloud(V)))) -> Prop
grammar.rule: This source-account reading names the excessive heat H as the dispersing/preventing agent. It preserves both dispersion and blocked cloud thickening. It does not assert that every excessive heat everywhere has that result; the explicit cES/report qualifiers remain. No winter lifting predicate is substituted here.

grammar.name: Material-to-goal transition
grammar.signature: MaterialKind TO GoalDescription -> TransitionDescription
grammar.rule: aiin shedaiin chok{co}m supplies ThickenToCloud(V): the goal description THICK_CLOUD_STATE contributes thickness and cloud, while TO contributes directed change. No event is asserted by this description. PREVENTS_TRANSITION makes precisely its non-achievement in the described generic account, retaining V and the explicit heat agent.

grammar.name: Shared raise head and two distinct failures
grammar.signature: OR HeatRef RAISE_REQUIREMENT QualifiedMaterial HeightGoal -> Coord[RaiseRequirement]
grammar.rule: This paid head-sharing syntax expands to exactly two written argument applications: R1=RaiseRequiredClass(H, Qualified(V,strong,firm,RequiredFor(THUNDER))) and R2=RaiseHighEnough(H,V,HeightGoal(V)). R2 carries the same thunder-relevant V restriction for the source pronoun, but has its own elevation goal. ARODY contributes sufficient height and violent downward descent, not an achieved descent. EACH_UNATTAINABLE maps the list to CannotAchieve(R1) AND CannotAchieve(R2); it is NOT merely NOT(R1 AND R2). No second actor, parcel, height number or sufficiency theorem is introduced.

grammar.name: Winter qualification and reference ownership
grammar.signature: RETURN_TO_OPENING + WINTER_REASON_ACCOUNT + ASSERT inability Prop -> InabilityClaim
grammar.rule: otchs selects the previously written c0. shedor restricts this account to WINTER. shedy reads HeatProfile(c0.region,WINTER), not cES heat. The independently written qodaiin odain in C09 must compute this same profile, and the equality is explicit in the manual derivation. The physical material is a generic kind; no cross-season parcel identity is claimed.

grammar.name: A contrasted reason account
grammar.signature: IN_CONTRAST_WITH Season BEGIN_ACCOUNT COORDINATE(ClaimRef BECAUSE heat-property ASSERT) -> Prop
grammar.rule: ypshedy dar supplies the summer comparison in the winter account. am reads the completed inability claim and its two written requirements. AN takes that requirement list as its explicit linked argument; it asserts MagnitudeInsufficientFor(computedWinterHeat,requirements). This projection from a written InabilityClaim is an additional paid interface, not a hidden arbitrary predicate inverse. chey asserts the completed reason. Because relates it to am; the unary or is charged as redundant coordination.

grammar.name: Explicit working place identification
grammar.signature: LOCATE_OPENING HERE US -> Prop
grammar.rule: orar oldar ain explicitly introduces rU (our region) and states r0=rU. This goes beyond the source, whose opening geography is unspecified. It is an admitted exploratory source departure, not retrospective source restoration. Earlier c0 references retain the same r0; no event moves and no heat value is measured.

grammar.name: Account-pattern collection
grammar.signature: Pattern(r,s) = the stated generic weather account at explicit context (r,s)
grammar.rule: AccountPattern is an intensional description, not a bag of physical events. grammar.name: Same-sort comparison
grammar.signature: LIKE: T x T -> Prop; T exactly HeatProfile or AccountPattern
grammar.rule: qokal has these two explicitly named type instantiations and no others. In C10, chdy and sary already denote AccountPatterns at AUTUMN/SPRING with the written current base region, so no Season-to-Pattern cast is hidden. In C11, ain olchey explicitly constructs SUMMER heat of US and compares it with shedy, the heat of cEW. Similarity is qualitative, not numerical equality. Thus C10 describes AUTUMN and SPRING by the WINTER exemplar; C11 describes EAST/WINTER by the US/SUMMER exemplar. Symmetry of LIKE is not assumed.

grammar.name: Postfixed thermal construction with explicit region

grammar.name: Western comparison with a thermal reason
grammar.signature: WEST_CASE ThemeRef HeatRef SIMILAR_REGIONAL_WEATHER RegionRef + MaterialRef BECAUSE_REGARDING THE HeatProperty DURING THE Season -> AttributedProp
grammar.rule: LOS introduces WEST and theme THUNDER. The final explicit SUMMER resolves this clause's season field. shedy therefore denotes HeatProfile(WEST,SUMMER). QOKSHEY compares the regional thunder account of that heat owner with US; it does not assert identity of all climates. OG takes V as an overt topic and relates the stated NotExcessive property of that same heat to the regional comparison. V is topic only: no western cloud-formation success or actual vapour event is silently inferred.

grammar.name: Question-answer recap

grammar.rule: ochar reselects the opening question and theme V. OTODY REQUIREMENTS forms RequirementSet(THUNDER). The remaining clause is the source-inspired logical recap in G29, not an extra meteorological datum. It is outside the SOME_SAY scope because OCHAR explicitly returns to the opening question.

grammar.name: Non-entailment of mere vapour ascent
grammar.signature: Requirements NOT_ENTAILED_BY_RISING_ALONE MaterialRef COORDINATE(RISING ACROSS MaterialRef CONTEXTS_OF) -> Prop
grammar.rule: ARAM builds exactly the opening winter/summer pair with the written V owner. AIROL makes the generic ascent premise across that pair; the unary OR is explicitly folded. OTEEDO checks that its named material equals the ascent's material, and states that this premise alone does not entail fulfillment of the thunder requirements. The extra argument check and recap are paid. It does not say that the stated requirements are jointly sufficient for thunder.

Source coverage means that those assertions are written inside the discourse act, not that ArgumentData is silently cast to Prop. CHEDY is an AccountHeader in BOTH C09 and C11; it creates the explicitly bounded body recorded below. No quotation of arbitrary operators, unknown controls, or empty body is admitted.
